about: Help for the Cranium phone apps. Every fact here comes from the repository; each topic lists where. Blocks: heading, text, steps, list, rows (label and text), note, see (other topics), links. The words follow the pages': plain words from the user's side, and no file, script, cloud service or ID outside the Developer section (cloud/web/test/copy.test.mjs checks it).

topics.title: Getting started
topics.summary: Signing in, and what a viewer and a release manager can do.

blocks.text: An administrator makes your account: there is no sign-up. The invitation e-mail has a temporary password that works for three days. At the first sign-in you choose a password and set up an authenticator app.
Sign in with your e-mail address, a password of at least 12 characters, and the code from your authenticator app.

rows: Sees everything: boards, releases, deployments, events and the activity log. Changes nothing.
Also uploads and revokes firmware, starts and cancels deployments, and sends a release to a board over Bluetooth.

blocks.text: An administrator gives or takes away the release manager role, and it counts at once. Your role is on More, Account.

topics.title: Why a change asks you to sign in again
topics.summary: A change from the phone needs a sign-in in the last 15 minutes.

blocks.text: A change made from the phone needs a sign-in, with password and code, in the last 15 minutes. So a phone left signed in cannot change anything hours later.
When your sign-in is older, the app asks you to sign in again, and then makes the change you asked for. If another account signs in instead, nothing is changed.

list: Looking never asks.
Standing at a board for an update over Bluetooth does not ask either.

topics.title: Unlocking with Face ID or your fingerprint
topics.summary: Face ID on an iPhone, your fingerprint on Android, instead of the password and code, for up to 30 days.

blocks.text: After you sign in with your password and code, the app can open with Face ID or Touch ID on an iPhone, or your fingerprint on Android, for up to 30 days.

steps: Sign in with your password and code.
Say yes when the app offers Face ID or your fingerprint, or turn it on later under More, Account.
From then on the app asks for it when it opens, and again after 5 minutes away.

blocks.heading: What still asks for the password and code

list: A change, such as an upload or a deployment, once the last full sign-in is over 15 minutes old. The console cannot see your phone's Face ID.
Face ID set up again, a new fingerprint added, or the phone's passcode turned off.
Signing out, or 30 days after the last full sign-in.

blocks.note: With it off, the app keeps you signed in for an hour after a sign-in.

topics.title: Keeping the app on your iPhone
topics.summary: A free Personal Team build stops opening after 7 days; renew.sh renews it.

blocks.text: An app signed by a free Personal Team installs on your own devices (at most 3), for 7 days at a time. After that it does not open until it is renewed. What it stored stays.
After the first install with Run in Xcode (apps/ios/scripts/phone.sh), the Mac can renew the app, by cable or over Wi-Fi:

rows: Every hour the Mac is awake, renew when 36 hours or less are left.
When the app stops opening, and whether the iPhone is in reach.

blocks.text: It builds the newest commit on main, so work in progress is never installed. Over Wi-Fi the iPhone has to be on the Mac's network, unlocked once since it restarted, and ticked Connect via network in Xcode, Window, Devices and Simulators. A failure shows a notification on the Mac; the log is ~/Library/Logs/cranium-renew.log.

topics.title: How an update over Wi-Fi works
topics.summary: The seven steps of a deployment, from the offer to the confirmed firmware.

blocks.text: A release manager deploys a release to one or more boards. A board on firmware 1.7.2 or newer starts as soon as it sees the offer, with nobody at the board. Older firmware waits for a press of Button 1; Button 2 declines.

steps: Offered: the console offers the update to the board.
Accepted by the board: the board checks that the update is newer than what it runs and fits.
Downloading: into the board's spare space. The firmware it runs is not touched.
Download checked: the board checks that the download is whole and is the release's. If not, it throws it away and installs nothing.
Restarting: the board checks the signature and starts the new firmware.
On trial: the new firmware has 5 minutes to join Wi-Fi and reach the console.
Confirmed: it reached the console, and is kept.

list: Not confirmed within 5 minutes: the board restarts into the firmware it had. The deployment says Rolled back.
A failed download is tried again, up to five times in all.
Ten minutes with no progress restart the board, with nothing installed.

topics.title: How an update over Bluetooth works
topics.summary: Hold Button 1 for 5 s, pair with the passkey, send, and press Button 1 to install.

blocks.text: For a board in the room, with Wi-Fi or without. Release managers only: the phone downloads the release and sends it to the board.

steps: At the board, hold Button 1 for five seconds and let go. LED1 shows four short flashes: Bluetooth is open for 3 minutes.
In the app, open Update over Bluetooth, pick a release, then the board. It shows as Cranium- and four letters or digits, new each time.
Type the 6-digit passkey into the phone's pairing prompt. When the board is online, the app shows it; otherwise it is on the board's serial console.

The app checks with the console that the release can still be sent, then sends it. Without the console's yes nothing is sent, also when the console cannot be reached. Keep the phone near the board, and the app open.
When it has arrived, LED1 blinks fast. Press Button 1 within two minutes to install it; Button 2 throws it away, and with no press it is erased.
The board restarts and runs the new firmware on trial.

list: A board takes one update each time Bluetooth is open, and only a newer version than it runs.
Each attempt has a new passkey. Three failed attempts close Bluetooth.
A phone that does not finish pairing is dropped after 45 s, and a connection with nothing happening after 120 s.
Button 2 closes Bluetooth at any point.

blocks.text: The new firmware is kept only if, within five minutes, it shows it can take a further update. If not, the board goes back to the firmware it had.

rows: It reaches the console. Nobody has to do anything.
After a minute, hold Button 1 and connect the phone again with a new passkey. The app does the rest.

blocks.text: A board's page shows its last update over Bluetooth and how it was kept.

topics.title: Deployments
topics.summary: One release offered to a set of boards, and where each board stands.

blocks.text: A deployment sends one release to a set of boards. Each board's part shows the seven steps of its update, live.
A board on firmware 1.7.2 or newer starts a deployment on its own. Older firmware waits for someone to press Button 1 on the board.

blocks.note: An update started outside the console is not listed here; its board's page shows it.

rows: Boards that have not started no longer get it. A board already downloading or installing finishes.
A board that is downloading or checking stops before installing. A board already restarting cannot be stopped.

blocks.text: A cancellation cannot be undone: to try again, start a new deployment. A board takes one deployment at a time.

topics.title: What a board's state means
topics.summary: Online, on trial, confirmed, rolled back, stuck restarts, revoked releases.

rows: It reported in the last 90 s. A board reports every 30 s, and one that said it is restarting stays online for 240 s.
No report for 90 s. The app shows what it last reported.
Has not reported to the console yet.
The firmware it runs has proved itself, and is kept.
New firmware is running and has not confirmed yet. If the board restarts first, it goes back to the firmware it had.
The new firmware did not reach the console in time, so the board went back to the firmware it had.
It can no longer be deployed, its open deployments are cancelled, and boards refuse it. Boards that already run it keep it until you deploy a newer version.
The board runs a version that is not in the list of releases.

blocks.text: From firmware 1.7.0 a stuck board restarts itself, but never while new firmware is on trial or Bluetooth is open.

rows: No connection to the cloud for 15 minutes
Wi-Fi is up, and the console cannot be reached.

blocks.text: Restarts in a row wait longer each time: about 2 minutes, 5 minutes, 30 minutes and 2 hours, then about four a day.
Firmware 1.5.0 is the golden image: one a person can always go back to at the board, with no laptop, Wi-Fi or cloud. The board keeps its name, Wi-Fi and certificates.

steps: Press and hold RESET.
Press and hold Button 2.
Let go of RESET.
Keep holding for 5 s, until LED1 blinks fast.
Let go of Button 2 within the next 5 s.

topics.title: What the board's LEDs mean
topics.summary: LED1's blink patterns, and LED2 taking turns with it when online.

blocks.text: LED1 shows what the board is doing, in a cycle of two seconds. From firmware 1.8.0, LED2 lights only when the board is online, taking turns with LED1.

rows: One second on, one off: joining Wi-Fi.
Half a second on, half off: Wi-Fi is up, connecting to the console.
New firmware is running on trial.
An update waits for a press of Button 1.
Bluetooth is open, and no phone is connected yet.
Set up, but not provisioned yet.

blocks.note: The board's other LEDs are not Cranium's.

topics.title: The board's buttons
topics.summary: Button 1 opens Bluetooth; holding Button 2 for 5 s is a factory reset.

rows: Opens Bluetooth for three minutes, for an update from a phone.
Installs an update that is waiting at the board.
Throws away or declines a waiting update, and closes Bluetooth.
Factory reset: the board forgets its name, Wi-Fi and certificates, and starts in factory mode. Not while an update is under way.

blocks.note: From firmware 1.7.2, an update over Wi-Fi needs no button.

topics.title: Boards and diagnostics
topics.summary: What a board's page shows: heartbeat, signal, memory, restarts and history.

blocks.text: Every board of this project, as it last reported. From firmware 1.11.4 a board shows its own device ID, with its thing name under it.

rows: Every 30 s. The page refreshes every 10 s, the charts every minute.
Wi-Fi strength: Excellent from −55 dBm, Good from −67, Fair from −75, Weak below.
Free memory now, and the least since the board started. Below 15% free is low.
Wi-Fi channel and memory, every 5 minutes, from firmware 1.10.0.
Why each start before ended, from firmware 1.7.4.
Its result and how it was kept, from firmware 1.9.0.
Each belongs to this board alone, and its private key never leaves the board.

topics.title: Firmware and signing
topics.summary: Signed releases, how the console checks them, and revoking.

blocks.text: Signed firmware that can be offered to boards. A version, once used, is never used again.

steps: Signed when it is built, with the project's private key.
Checked on upload by the console, with the public key.
Checked again by the board when it starts.

blocks.text: The console keeps only firmware whose signature matches this project's key. It holds only the public half of the key, so it can check a signature but never make one.

list: It stops downloading at once, and every unfinished deployment of it is cancelled.
It can never be deployed again, and its version stays used.
Boards that run it keep it until you deploy a newer version.
It cannot be undone.

topics.title: Events
topics.summary: What every board did, as it reported it, kept for 90 days.

blocks.text: What every board did, as it reported it, with what people did in the console alongside. Events are kept for 90 days.

rows: A band is a board online.

blocks.text: A range that ends now refreshes every 15 s. A range you choose may be at most 31 days.

topics.title: The activity log
topics.summary: Every change made through the console, with who asked for it.

blocks.text: Every upload, deployment, cancellation and revocation made through the console, with who asked for it and whether it went through. Nobody can change an entry.

topics.title: API tokens
topics.summary: Tokens that let a script use the console as you.

blocks.text: A token lets a script use the console's API as you, without signing in, until it expires or you revoke it. Each person makes and sees only their own.

list: Send it as Authorization: Bearer crn_… to the API under /api/t/.
scripts/firmware/ota.sh uses the token in ~/.cranium/console-token (chmod 600), or in CRANIUM_TOKEN.
It may do what you may do at that moment: a viewer's token only reads.
A change made with it is in the activity log under your name, with the token's ID.
It cannot make or revoke tokens, or read a board's Bluetooth passkey.
It is shown once. Valid for 1 to 90 days; it cannot be extended.

topics.title: The serial console
topics.summary: Driving a board on its USB cable: where it works, and how the commands look.

blocks.text: The serial console drives a board on its USB cable, one command per line. What you type goes to the board, never to the server, and nothing is saved.

rows: In Chrome or Edge on a computer, for release managers. It drives a board directly and can erase it.
On a phone that can be a USB host (USB OTG). Android asks you to allow the app to use the board.
The board's second virtual COM port, at 115200 baud: screen /dev/cu.usbmodem<port> 115200
iOS lets no app open a USB serial port, so it has no serial console.

list: One command per line, like COMMAND|arg1|arg2. HELP or ? lists them, with the firmware version.
Every command ends with one line: OK, or ERR and the reason.
Lines that start with a [TAG] are logs, such as [BT] passkey 123456 while a phone pairs.

blocks.note: A release build can leave the console out (-Dapp_CONFIG_APP_CONSOLE=n): then no serial command exists.

topics.title: A board is offline
topics.summary: No report for 90 s: what to check.

list: A board counts as offline 90 s after its last report. An open page can take about two minutes to show it.
Usually it is the Wi-Fi: the hotspot is off, or its name differs by a character. Give it a few minutes.
Never connected: power it up and check that it was provisioned.
To send it the Wi-Fi network again, connect it by USB: see Sending the Wi-Fi network again, under Developer.
A board that never comes online: its certificate must be attached to it. Its page lists its certificates.
From firmware 1.7.0 a stuck board restarts itself.

topics.title: Bluetooth can't find the board
topics.summary: Opening Bluetooth, the passkey, and a refused or broken send.

rows: Bluetooth is not open, or closed after 3 minutes. Hold Button 1 for 5 s, then look again.
A wrong passkey. Three failures close Bluetooth: open it again and use the new passkey.
Not newer than what the board runs, or one was already sent this time. Pick a newer release, or open Bluetooth again.
Out of range, or Bluetooth closed. Open it again and send again.
The release was revoked, or it is not the release's firmware. Nothing was sent.
Bluetooth is off or not allowed
Turn it on, and allow Cranium to use Bluetooth in the phone's settings.

topics.title: The upload was refused
topics.summary: What the console checks, and what each refusal means.

blocks.text: The console keeps only firmware built for this board, signed with this project's key, and newer than every release before it, revoked ones included.

rows: Versions only go up. The refusal names the highest so far.
This file, or another with the same version, is a release already.
Signed with another key than this project's.
It must fit the board's space for an update.
Never accepted: give the build a version first.
Choose the signed file from the build.

blocks.text: Nothing was stored. Choose another file.

topics.title: Sign-in problems
topics.summary: Password and code, locked accounts, a lost phone, a missing role.

list: A password of at least 12 characters, and the code from your authenticator app.
Repeated wrong passwords lock an account for a while.
Lost phone or password: an administrator resets both, and your role stays.
An account removed, disabled or without a role cannot sign in: ask an administrator.
A change refused as not allowed: you are not a release manager. Ask an administrator for the role.
